source_text.body:
Run a real estate CRM workflow with Claude Code
A real estate broker feeds Claude Code notes, emails and photos so it writes listing copy, qualifies and splits leads, runs market analysis, updates CRM records and schedules tasks.
·
Mar 11, 2026
Done with
CC
Claude Code
What they did
A real estate broker set up Claude Code with a large folder of interconnected markdown “skills” that tell it how to handle listing writeups, lead qualification and routing, market analysis, and deal processing. Each evening the broker dumps in PLAUD note transcriptions, emails, SMS/iMessages, and property photos; Claude reads the batch, writes structured summaries into client CRM.md files, creates prioritized follow-up tasks, schedules calendar items, and updates Google Contacts.
How it went
The post says Claude became the broker’s main workflow brain and keeps a better overview of the work than the broker does. The source gives no hard performance numbers, and the comments mostly discuss similar setups rather than reporting measured results or failures.
Worth knowing
The main catch is the up-front system: the broker says the skills library is thousands of lines of markdown, and the routine runs as one end-of-day batch session.
Try it yourself
with
Claude Code
Copy prompt
I'm a real estate broker. Using the notes, emails, and photos in [folder path], write listing copy for [property address], sort incoming leads into [qualified, nurture, not a fit] with reasons, and update my CRM records in [CRM file or export]. You're done when the listing copy and updated lead list are saved in [output folder] with follow-up tasks listed by date. Show me any emails or CRM changes before sending or saving them.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/ClaudeCode/comments/1rr9my9/does_anyone_else_use_claude_code_as_their_actual
